title: Twigg configuration
description: Instructions, tools, context budgets and retention for an organisation and its namespaces, applied with `twigg config apply`. A scope or surface left out is unmanaged and never changed; `null` withdraws its override so it inherits from the parent.

global.description: The organisation-wide scope every namespace inherits from.

namespaces.description: Namespace scopes, keyed by namespace. Children inherit from their parents: `acme/support` resolves on top of `acme`.

FileReference.description: Load this value from a file, relative to the configuration file. Markdown or text for instructions; JSON or YAML for structured values.

retain.description: How recent a part must be for media of this type to be replayed.

MediaRules.description: The media section: which attachments are replayed.

RetentionRules.description: The stored document. Private fields: holding one is proof it parsed.

anchor_parts.description:
How many parts at the head of the chat are pinned verbatim, never
compacted and never truncated. `0` disables it.

Counted in **parts**, not tokens, because the value a customer wants to
express is "the task spec", which is a part boundary they can see — not a
token count they would have to estimate and re-tune whenever they edited
the spec.

reasoning.description:
How recent a part must be for its reasoning to be replayed. Defaults to
the same window as media: a reasoning block's replay token is worthless
to a model of another family anyway, and old reasoning is the least
load-bearing, most expensive thing in a long agentic history.

verbatim_within.description:
How recent a payload must be to escape truncation entirely — tool results,
tool arguments and prose alike.

One setting for the whole document, deliberately, and the direct
descendant of the old `truncate_within_frontier` flag. "Don't cut the tool
output I just received" is not a per-tool judgement, and giving each
family its own would put three definitions of "recent" back in a document
whose entire point is that there is one.

Hoisted out of the tool section when prose truncation arrived: the
alternative was a second identical field on `TextRules`, which is how a
shared metric quietly becomes two that drift.

instructions.description: System instructions. A bare string or file reference publishes with mode `append`. `null` withdraws this scope's instructions.

tools.description: Saved tools. `null` withdraws this scope's tool bundle.

budgets.description: Context budgets. `null` withdraws every budget in this scope.

retention.description: Retention policy. `null` withdraws this scope's policy.

ScopeBudgets.description: Keyed by `default` (the budget for every model without its own) or a catalogue model name such as `claude-opus-5`. `null` withdraws that key's budget.

mode.description: How this scope combines with its parent. Defaults to `append`; ignored on the global scope.
How this scope combines with its parent. Defaults to `append`.

TextRules.description: Truncation policies for older user prompts and assistant messages. The current exchange and configured anchor remain protected.

message.description:
Applied to an assistant `message`'s text.

Separate from `prompt` for the same reason a tool's arguments and result
are separate: they are different sizes with different value. A customer
pasting logs wants their own input cut; a customer whose model writes long
answers wants the replies cut.

TokenEstimate.description:
A count of estimated tokens. Always non-negative; saturates rather than
overflowing, because a budget calculation must never wrap into a small
number and wave through a request that cannot fit.

ToolDefinition.description: A named tool with a description and JSON Schema parameters. Parameters must be a valid schema describing an object; external schema references are not supported.

strict.description:
Ask the provider to guarantee the tool call validates against the schema.

`None` means the customer did not say, which is distinct from `false`:
the providers' own defaults differ, and translating an unstated
preference into an explicit `false` would silently opt a customer out of
a guarantee they never declined. Dropped when targeting Google, which has
no equivalent.

ToolRules.description: The tool section: how tool payloads are cut down.

oneOf.description:
Replaces the matched `result` treatment on a part flagged `is_error`.
`None` means errors follow the ordinary rule.

Worth its own knob because failures split the customer base cleanly: for
one, a stack trace is the most valuable thing in the history; for the
next, it is a retry loop's worth of noise.

mark_truncations.description:
Whether a cut payload carries a visible marker of what was elided.

Defaults **on**, and deliberately not a per-rule choice: a model that
cannot tell output was truncated will confidently invent the missing
middle, and that failure is not a per-tool judgement call.

ToolTreatment.description:
How one tool's two payloads are treated. Arguments and results are separate
because they are separate parts with separate sizes — a `write_file` call's
arguments routinely dwarf its result, and a `search` call's result dwarfs its
arguments.

Truncation.description: Keep content unchanged, always truncate to a token target, or truncate only when it exceeds a threshold. Choose the head, tail, or both ends to retain.

TruncationOver.description:
Cut to `to` tokens, but only once the payload exceeds `over`. The common
shape: small results replay verbatim, a runaway one is clipped.
